sentences.text: Mirjul Bhangi vs The State Of West Bengal on 7 August, 2025

Sl. no. 12
Ct. No. 25
 P.M.
 C.R.A. (Sb) 105 Of 2025

Mirjul Bhangi
 - Vs -
 The State of West Bengal.

Mr. Sabir Ahmed,,
 Mr. Sudip Kushri,
 Mr. Tasnim Ahamed,
 Mr. Dhiman Banerjee
 .... For the appellant

1. 
The present appeal has been filed challenging the judgement of conviction dated 19 th May, 2025 and order of sentence dated 20.05.2025 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge, 6 th Court,
Paschim Medinipur.

entities.text:
Additional Sessions Judge, 6 th Court,
Paschim Medinipur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The appellant has been convicted for the offence under Section 306/498A of Indian Penal Code and has been awarded rigorous imprisonment for five years and two years respectively.

The appellant has also been paid in course of forty thousand in default of which rigorous imprisonment for ten months for the offence under Section 306 of Indian Penal Code and fine of Rs. 10,000/- in default simple imprisonment for three months for the offence under section 498A of IPC.
2. The appeal has been filed in time.

3. The learned counsel for the appellant states that the learned Trial Court has filed it by ignoring material contradiction and taking into account the fact that the grounds of "abatement" as a defence under Section 106 were not made out.
4. The appeal is admitted.

5. Let the appellant be filed properly authenticated copy of the learned trial court judgement.
6.
Issue notice to the office of the Public Prosecutor.

7. Let the nominal role be called for from the Superintendent Midnapore Central Correctional Home satisfying the period of sentence already undergone and the conduct of the appellant.
8.
Liberty is granted to file the application for bail.

9. Let the Trial Court records be called for.
